provider: infosec.exchange — Mastodon with a 1.35 GiB per-file upload limit (highest single-object cap found anywhere in the fediverse)

free_tier.stated: Per-account storage is UNLIMITED (stock Mastodon has no per-user media quota at all. Media_attachment has only a per-file size validator, no account-level counter). Per FILE: image_size_limit = video_size_limit = 1419430400 bytes = 1.32 GiB. That is a 84x relaxation of Mastodon's compiled defaults (IMAGE_LIMIT 16 MB / VIDEO_LIMIT 99 MB).
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: Per FILE: image_size_limit = video_size_limit = 1419430400 bytes = 1.32 GiB
per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: infosec.exchange is one of the largest and best-funded Mastodon instances (Glitch fork 4.8.0-alpha.3) and explicitly runs a relaxed upload policy; still a single volunteer operator, and a 1.3 GiB upload is exactly the kind of thing that gets noticed. Media is permanent by Mastodon semantics (no TTL, no GC), which cuts both ways.

egress.terms: Free. No egress meter on the instance; media sits behind the instance CDN (often S3/Wasabi/B2-compatible behind a CNAME).

tooling: Mastodon REST API v1: POST /api/v1/media (multipart `file` -> returns media id + `url`), then POST /api/v1/statuses with media_ids[] to make it permanent. OAuth2 app registration via POST /api/v1/apps (no manual approval on most instances). Any of the many existing clients work; `toot` CLI, `Mastodon.py`. Upload-from-URL: POST /api/v2/media with `url` param. rclone has no Mastodon backend but the API is 3 calls.
chaining: The key structural fact: NO per-account quota means the ceiling is the instance's disk, and the operator absorbs it. Combined with a 1.32 GiB per-file cap and 8 attachments per status, one status carries 10.6 GiB in a single API call chain. Multiple accounts on the same instance each get the same unlimited-account treatment. Multiply over instances for isolation.

limits.value: Per FILE: image_size_limit = video_size_limit = 1419430400 bytes = 1.32 GiB

limits_note: Request-rate is THE binding limit, and it is severe: stock Mastodon rack_attack ships `throttle('throttle_api_media', limit: 30, period: 30.minutes)` per authenticated user. 30 media uploads per half hour = 1,440/day. At 1.32 GiB each that is a theoretical 1.9 TB/day/account, so realistically you hit GB-scale throughput only by running many accounts in parallel. Also: 8 media per status (MAX_MEDIA_ATTACHMENTS), 4 statuses/30 min soft on some instances, MAX_VIDEO_FRAMES 36,000 (≈5 min at 120 fps) and MAX_VIDEO_MATRIX_LIMIT 8,294,400 px cap video dimensions, and non-image/video MIME types are rejected by the upload validator.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
